[user]
=== Red3 Duel ===

CARDS. There are 21 cards: numbers 1 to 7 in each of 3 colours, Red, Green and Violet. Colour rank is Red 3, Green 2, Violet 1. A card's strength is number x 10 + colour rank (7 Red = 73, 4 Violet = 41). Higher strength beats lower. A card is EVEN if its number is 2, 4 or 6. A card is LOW if its number is 3 or less.

THE RULE. The Canvas shows one colour, which is the current rule (canvas 3 = Red, 2 = Green, 1 = Violet). Each living player has a KEY under the current rule:
- Red: key = strength of the highest card in your palette.
- Green: key = 100 x (number of even cards in your palette) + strength of your highest even card, or 0 if you have no even card.
- Violet: key = 100 x (number of low cards in your palette) + strength of your highest low card, or 0 if you have no low card.
You are LEADING if your key is strictly higher than every other living player's key. If keys tie, including at 0, no tied player is leading.

SETUP OF A HAND. Shuffle all 21 cards. Deal each player 5 cards as a hidden hand, then 1 card face up as their palette. The remaining cards (9 with 2 players, 3 with 3 players) are set aside unseen for this hand. The Canvas starts as Red. Everyone is alive. The initial leader is the player whose palette card has the highest strength. The first turn of the hand goes to the next player in seat order after that leader.

A TURN. On your turn choose exactly one:
(a) play one card from your hand face up to your palette;
(b) discard one card from your hand to the Canvas, so the rule becomes that card's colour and the card leaves play;
(c) do (a), then (b), with two different cards;

- With 3 players: the hand winner scores 2 points; the player whose elimination left one survivor scores 1; the first player eliminated scores 0.

- With 2 players, the match ends when a player reaches 3 points.
- With 3 players, the match ends after any hand in which a player reaches 6 or more points.

- **Why it works now:** Under Green, it gives me 2 even cards (4 Red and 6 Violet), with 6 Violet (61) as my highest. My key becomes 261, which beats the opponent's 242.
- **What the opponent can do:** They cannot win under Red, because my 7 Red (73) is the top card. If they switch to Violet without adding even cards, I can play 1 Violet and discard 1 Green. That puts the rule back to Green, where my 261 still beats their 242. Their best counter is to play another even card while Green stays the rule.
- **Why not discard 4 Red:** That makes Red the rule, but they can then switch to Green or Violet. I would be stuck with only 1 Green and 1 Violet, and could not get the lead back.

play 4 Red

=== Red3 Duel ===

CARDS. There are 21 cards: numbers 1 to 7 in each of 3 colours, Red, Green and Violet. Colour rank is Red 3, Green 2, Violet 1. A card's strength is number x 10 + colour rank (7 Red = 73, 4 Violet = 41). Higher strength beats lower. A card is EVEN if its number is 2, 4 or 6. A card is LOW if its number is 3 or less.

THE RULE. The Canvas shows one colour, which is the current rule (canvas 3 = Red, 2 = Green, 1 = Violet). Each living player has a KEY under the current rule:
- Red: key = strength of the highest card in your palette.
- Green: key = 100 x (number of even cards in your palette) + strength of your highest even card, or 0 if you have no even card.
- Violet: key = 100 x (number of low cards in your palette) + strength of your highest low card, or 0 if you have no low card.
You are LEADING if your key is strictly higher than every other living player's key. If keys tie, including at 0, no tied player is leading.

SETUP OF A HAND. Shuffle all 21 cards. Deal each player 5 cards as a hidden hand, then 1 card face up as their palette. The remaining cards (9 with 2 players, 3 with 3 players) are set aside unseen for this hand. The Canvas starts as Red. Everyone is alive. The initial leader is the player whose palette card has the highest strength. The first turn of the hand goes to the next player in seat order after that leader.

A TURN. On your turn choose exactly one:
(a) play one card from your hand face up to your palette;
(b) discard one card from your hand to the Canvas, so the rule becomes that card's colour and the card leaves play;
(c) do (a), then (b), with two different cards;
(d) fold.
Then keys are recomputed under the current rule. If you are leading, you stay alive and play goes on. If you are not leading, or you folded, you are eliminated from the hand: your palette stays visible but no longer counts. If you have no cards left in hand when your turn comes, you can only fold. Play passes to the next living player in seat order.

A ROUND is one pass of turns through all living players in seat order, starting with the player whose turn it is.

END OF A HAND. A hand ends the moment only one player is alive. That player is the hand winner and becomes the most recent hand winner.
- With 2 players: the hand winner scores 1 point; the other scores 0.
- With 3 players: the hand winner scores 2 points; the player whose elimination left one survivor scores 1; the first player eliminated scores 0.
If the match is not over, a new hand is set up at the start of the next round.

END OF THE MATCH.
- With 2 players, the match ends when a player reaches 3 points.
- With 3 players, the match ends after any hand in which a player reaches 6 or more points.

=== Red3 Duel ===

CARDS. There are 21 cards: numbers 1 to 7 in each of 3 colours, Red, Green and Violet. Colour rank is Red 3, Green 2, Violet 1. A card's strength is number x 10 + colour rank (7 Red = 73, 4 Violet = 41). Higher strength beats lower. A card is EVEN if its number is 2, 4 or 6. A card is LOW if its number is 3 or less.

THE RULE. The Canvas shows one colour, which is the current rule (canvas 3 = Red, 2 = Green, 1 = Violet). Each living player has a KEY under the current rule:
- Red: key = strength of the highest card in your palette.
- Green: key = 100 x (number of even cards in your palette) + strength of your highest even card, or 0 if you have no even card.
- Violet: key = 100 x (number of low cards in your palette) + strength of your highest low card, or 0 if you have no low card.
You are LEADING if your key is strictly higher than every other living player's key. If keys tie, including at 0, no tied player is leading.

SETUP OF A HAND. Shuffle all 21 cards. Deal each player 5 cards as a hidden hand, then 1 card face up as their palette. The remaining cards (9 with 2 players, 3 with 3 players) are set aside unseen for this hand. The Canvas starts as Red. Everyone is alive. The initial leader is the player whose palette card has the highest strength. The first turn of the hand goes to the next player in seat order after that leader.

A TURN. On your turn choose exactly one:
(a) play one card from your hand face up to your palette;
(b) discard one card from your hand to the Canvas, so the rule becomes that card's colour and the card leaves play;
(c) do (a), then (b), with two different cards;
(d) fold.
Then keys are recomputed under the current rule. If you are leading, you stay alive and play goes on. If you are not leading, or you folded, you are eliminated from the hand: your palette stays visible but no longer counts. If you have no cards left in hand when your turn comes, you can only fold. Play passes to the next living player in seat order.

A ROUND is one pass of turns through all living players in seat order, starting with the player whose turn it is.

END OF A HAND. A hand ends the moment only one player is alive. That player is the hand winner and becomes the most recent hand winner.
- With 2 players: the hand winner scores 1 point; the other scores 0.
- With 3 players: the hand winner scores 2 points; the player whose elimination left one survivor scores 1; the first player eliminated scores 0.
If the match is not over, a new hand is set up at the start of the next round.

END OF THE MATCH.
- With 2 players, the match ends when a player reaches 3 points.
- With 3 players, the match ends after any hand in which a player reaches 6 or more points.
- In either case, it also ends when round 40 is complete; an unfinished hand then scores nothing.

INFORMATION. Palettes, the Canvas, eliminations, points and the most recent hand winner are public. Hands and set-aside cards are hidden. There is no table talk.

WINNING. The player with the most points when the match ends wins. If two or more players share the most points, the tied player who won the most recently completed hand wins. If no hand was completed at all, the match is a draw with no winner.

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.

[user]
=== Red3 Duel ===

CARDS. There are 21 cards: numbers 1 to 7 in each of 3 colours, Red, Green and Violet. Colour rank is Red 3, Green 2, Violet 1. A card's strength is number x 10 + colour rank (7 Red = 73, 4 Violet = 41). Higher strength beats lower. A card is EVEN if its number is 2, 4 or 6. A card is LOW if its number is 3 or less.

THE RULE. The Canvas shows one colour, which is the current rule (canvas 3 = Red, 2 = Green, 1 = Violet). Each living player has a KEY under the current rule:
- Red: key = strength of the highest card in your palette.
- Green: key = 100 x (number of even cards in your palette) + strength of your highest even card, or 0 if you have no even card.
- Violet: key = 100 x (number of low cards in your palette) + strength of your highest low card, or 0 if you have no low card.
You are LEADING if your key is strictly higher than every other living player's key. If keys tie, including at 0, no tied player is leading.

SETUP OF A HAND. Shuffle all 21 cards. Deal each player 5 cards as a hidden hand, then 1 card face up as their palette. The remaining cards (9 with 2 players, 3 with 3 players) are set aside unseen for this hand. The Canvas starts as Red. Everyone is alive. The initial leader is the player whose palette card has the highest strength. The first turn of the hand goes to the next player in seat order after that leader.

A TURN. On your turn choose exactly one:
(a) play one card from your hand face up to your palette;
(b) discard one card from your hand to the Canvas, so the rule becomes that card's colour and the card leaves play;
(c) do (a), then (b), with two different cards;
(d) fold.
Then keys are recomputed under the current rule. If you are leading, you stay alive and play goes on. If you are not leading, or you folded, you are eliminated from the hand: your palette stays visible but no longer counts. If you have no cards left in hand when your turn comes, you can only fold. Play passes to the next living player in seat order.

A ROUND is one pass of turns through all living players in seat order, starting with the player whose turn it is.

END OF A HAND. A hand ends the moment only one player is alive. That player is the hand winner and becomes the most recent hand winner.
- With 2 players: the hand winner scores 1 point; the other scores 0.
- With 3 players: the hand winner scores 2 points; the player whose elimination left one survivor scores 1; the first player eliminated scores 0.
If the match is not over, a new hand is set up at the start of the next round.

END OF THE MATCH.
- With 2 players, the match ends when a player reaches 3 points.
- With 3 players, the match ends after any hand in which a player reaches 6 or more points.
- In either case, it also ends when round 40 is complete; an unfinished hand then scores nothing.

INFORMATION. Palettes, the Canvas, eliminations, points and the most recent hand winner are public. Hands and set-aside cards are hidden. There is no table talk.

WINNING. The player with the most points when the match ends wins. If two or more players share the most points, the tied player who won the most recently completed hand wins. If no hand was completed at all, the match is a draw with no winner.

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
